source.text: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having passed the Sabbath, Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of James and Salome bought spices so that having come they might anoint him.

en.L: And when the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of James and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: After the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome purchased spices so that they could go and anoint {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.
en.R: The Sabbath day ended. Then three women bought sweet-smelling spices: Mary from Magdala, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. They wanted to go and put them on Jesus' body.

es.L: Y pasado el sábado, María Magdalena y María la [madre] de Santiago y Salomé compraron aromas para que, viniendo, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ungieran.
es.B: Pasado el sábado, María Magdalena, María la madre de Santiago, y Salomé compraron perfumes para ir a ungir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo.
es.R: Terminó el sábado. Entonces tres mujeres compraron perfumes de olor agradable: María, la de Magdala, María, la madre de Santiago, y Salomé. Querían ir a ponerlos sobre el cuerpo de Jesús.

sw.L: Na baada ya Sabato kupita, Mariamu Magdalene, na Mariamu [mama] wa Yakobo, na Salome walinunua manukato ili, wakiisha kufika, wampake.
sw.B: Siku ya Sabato ilipomalizika, Mariamu Magdalene, Mariamu mama wa Yakobo, na Salome walinunua manukato ili waende kuupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato ilipokwisha, wanawake watatu walinunua manukato yenye harufu nzuri: Mariamu wa Magdala, Mariamu mama wa Yakobo, na Salome. Walitaka kwenda kuupaka mwili wa Yesu manukato hayo.

decisions.choice: when the Sabbath was over: after sunset on Saturday, when the Sabbath ended and shops could open
decisions.reason: The Jewish day ended at sunset. Jesus died on the day before the Sabbath (15:42), so the women could buy spices only on Saturday evening.

decisions.choice: Mary of James: the mother of James, as in 15:40
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of James". Mark 15:40 names her as the mother of James the younger and of Joses.

decisions.choice: spices to anoint him: fragrant oils poured on a body as a last honor
decisions.reason: Jews did not embalm. Spiced oils honored the dead and masked the smell of decay. Jesus had been buried in haste (15:46), and he had said that the woman at Bethany anointed his body beforehand for burial (14:8).

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene: Mary from Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: She watched the crucifixion and the burial (15:40, 15:47).

decisions.choice: his body (B); Jesus' body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the women came to honor a dead body. Readable also says "from Magdala" and "sweet-smelling" to explain the name and the spices.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: lo (L), su (B)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("vive", "se apareció") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("ungirlo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English; Literal says "lo ungieran" so the pronoun can carry it. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: aromas (L); perfumes (B, R)
decisions.reason: The spices were fragrant oils and ointments to put on the body (meaning decision m3). "Perfumes" says that; "especias" sounds like dry spices for cooking.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on wampake (that they might anoint him); a span on wake (his) at Balanced
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -m- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου.

records.literal_gloss: And very early on the first [day] of the week they come to the tomb, having risen the sun.

en.L: And very early on the first [day] of the week they come to the tomb, when the sun had risen.
en.B: On the first day of the week, very early, when the sun had come up, they came to the tomb.
en.R: Very early on Sunday morning, just after the sun came up, they went to the tomb.

es.L: Y muy temprano, el primer [día] de la semana, llegan al sepulcro, cuando el sol ya había salido.
es.B: El primer día de la semana, muy de madrugada, apenas salido el sol, fueron al sepulcro.
es.R: El domingo, muy temprano, justo después de salir el sol, fueron a la tumba.

sw.L: Na mapema sana siku ya kwanza ya juma wanakuja kaburini, jua likiwa limechomoza.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya juma, asubuhi na mapema kabisa, mara jua lilipochomoza, walifika kaburini.
sw.R: Jumapili asubuhi na mapema sana, mara tu baada ya jua kuchomoza, walikwenda kaburini.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: Sunday, the day after the Sabbath
alternatives: the first day of a feast
decisions.reason: The Jewish week ended with the Sabbath, so the next day was the first day of the week. Christians later met on this day because Jesus rose on it.

decisions.choice: they come: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they came.

decisions.choice: very early, when the sun had risen: at dawn, as the sun was coming up
decisions.reason: "Very early" and "the sun having risen" together point to the first light of day.

decisions.choice: Sunday morning
alternatives: the first day of the week
decisions.reason: Readable names the day for readers who do not know the Jewish week.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (llegan); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (fueron)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this passage in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 4 and 6.

decisions.choice: sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 20: "sepulcro" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "tumba" at Readable. The same through verse 8.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanakuja); past at Balanced and Readable (walifika, walikwenda)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this passage in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 4 and 6.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς· Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου;

records.literal_gloss: And they were saying to themselves, Who will roll away for us the stone from the door of the tomb?

en.L: And they were saying to one another, "Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?"
en.B: They had been asking each other, "Who is going to roll the stone back from the entrance to the tomb for us?"
en.R: On the way they kept asking each other, "Who will move the stone away from the opening of the tomb for us?"

es.L: Y se decían entre ellas: «¿Quién nos apartará la piedra de la puerta del sepulcro?».
es.B: Se preguntaban unas a otras: «¿Quién nos va a correr la piedra de la entrada del sepulcro?».
es.R: Por el camino se preguntaban unas a otras: «¿Quién nos va a quitar la piedra de la entrada de la tumba?».

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakiambiana, "Nani atatuvingirishia jiwe kutoka mlangoni mwa kaburi?"
sw.B: Walikuwa wakiulizana, "Ni nani atakayetuvingirishia jiwe hilo kutoka kwenye mlango wa kaburi?"
sw.R: Njiani waliendelea kuulizana, "Ni nani atakayetusogezea jiwe mbali na mlango wa kaburi?"

decisions.choice: the stone at the door: a large stone that closed the opening of a tomb cut in rock
alternatives: a small stone marking the grave
decisions.reason: Joseph had rolled such a stone against the entrance (15:46). It took several men to move.

decisions.choice: they were saying: they kept asking as they went
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: it was their worry all the way to the tomb.

decisions.choice: On the way they kept asking
decisions.reason: Readable sets the question on the road to the tomb, as the continuous verb implies.

source.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀποκεκύλισται ὁ λίθος, ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked up they see that has been rolled away the stone; it was for large extremely.

en.L: And looking up, they see that the stone has been rolled away; for it was extremely large.
en.B: When they looked up, they could see the stone had already been rolled away, and it was a huge stone.
en.R: But then they looked up and saw that the stone had been moved away already. And it was a very big stone!

es.L: Y alzando la vista, ven que la piedra ha sido apartada; pues era sumamente grande.
es.B: Pero al levantar la vista vieron que la piedra ya había sido apartada, y era una piedra enorme.
es.R: Pero entonces miraron y vieron que ya habían movido la piedra. ¡Y era una piedra muy grande!

sw.L: Na walipotazama juu, wanaona kwamba jiwe limevingirishwa kando; maana lilikuwa kubwa kupita kiasi.
sw.B: Walipoinua macho, waliona kwamba jiwe lilikuwa tayari limevingirishwa kando. Na jiwe hilo lilikuwa kubwa sana.
sw.R: Lakini walipotazama juu, waliona kwamba jiwe lilikuwa limekwisha kusogezwa. Tena lilikuwa jiwe kubwa sana!

decisions.choice: for it was extremely large: explains their worry and why they could see from a distance that it had been moved
decisions.reason: Mark adds the note after the event. It looks back to the question of 16:3 and makes the opening of the tomb more striking.

decisions.choice: has been rolled away: a passive that does not name who moved it
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who rolled the stone. The passive leaves it to God's action, as the young man inside makes clear.

decisions.choice: rolled away, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have a related verb meaning rolled back or rolled up. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they see: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: The sense is past, as in 16:2.

decisions.choice: habían movido, with no subject
decisions.reason: The Greek passive does not say who moved the stone (meaning decision m2). The Spanish impersonal plural names no one either, as "habían quitado" in John 20:1.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν, καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered into the tomb they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a robe white, and they were greatly amazed.

en.L: And entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe, and they were utterly amazed.
en.B: On entering the tomb they found a young man seated on the right, wearing a white robe, and they were stunned.
en.R: They went into the tomb. A young man in a white robe was sitting there on the right side. The women were shocked and frightened.

es.L: Y entrando en el sepulcro, vieron a un joven sentado a la derecha, vestido con una túnica blanca, y quedaron sumamente asombradas.
es.B: Al entrar en el sepulcro encontraron a un joven sentado a la derecha, con una túnica blanca, y se quedaron atónitas.
es.R: Entraron en la tumba. Allí, a la derecha, estaba sentado un joven vestido con una túnica blanca. Las mujeres se quedaron asombradas y asustadas.

sw.L: Na walipoingia kaburini walimwona kijana ameketi upande wa kulia, amevikwa joho jeupe, nao wakashangaa sana.
sw.B: Walipoingia kaburini, walimkuta kijana ameketi upande wa kulia, akiwa amevaa joho jeupe, nao wakashtuka sana.
sw.R: Waliingia ndani ya kaburi. Kijana mmoja aliyevaa nguo ndefu nyeupe alikuwa ameketi pale upande wa kulia. Wale wanawake walishtuka, wakaogopa.

decisions.choice: a young man in a white robe: a messenger from God
alternatives: the young man who fled in 14:51-52
decisions.reason: White clothing marks heavenly beings (9:3; Daniel 7:9). Matthew 28:2-5 calls him an angel of the Lord, and Luke 24:4 speaks of two men in shining clothes. Mark says only "a young man"; some have linked him with the young man who fled in 14:51, but Mark does not.

decisions.choice: utterly amazed: overcome with awe and alarm
decisions.reason: The verb is strong. It is used of the crowd at 9:15 and of Jesus' distress in Gethsemane (14:33). Here it is fear and awe at once.

decisions.choice: on the right: the right side of the tomb as one enters
decisions.reason: A tomb cut in rock had a ledge or bench where the body was laid. The young man sits inside, to the right.

decisions.choice: shocked and frightened
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the strong verb, which joins awe and alarm.

decisions.choice: joho (L, B); nguo ndefu (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a long outer robe. "Joho" is that garment; "vazi" is any piece of clothing, and "kanzu" today names a particular men's gown. Readable describes it in plain words.

source.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς· Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε· Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον· ἠγέρθη, οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: He but says to them, Not be amazed; Jesus you seek the Nazarene, the [one] having been crucified; he was raised, not he is here; see the place where they laid him;

en.L: But he says to them, "Do not be amazed. You are seeking Jesus the Nazarene, the one who has been crucified. He has been raised; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not here. See the place where they laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But he told them, "Do not be alarmed. You have come looking for Jesus from Nazareth, the one who was crucified. He has been raised; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not here. Look, this is the place where they laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But he told them, "Do not be frightened. You are looking for Jesus from Nazareth, who was killed on a cross. God has raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from death! He is not here. Look, here is the place where they put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.

es.L: Pero él les dice: «No {{plural_you:se asombren|os asombréis}}. A Jesús el nazareno {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}, el que ha sido crucificado. Ha sido resucitado; no está aquí. {{plural_you:Vean|Ved}} el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} colocaron.
es.B: Pero él les dijo: «No {{plural_you:se alarmen|os alarméis}}. {{plural_you:Vienen|Venís}} buscando a Jesús de Nazaret, el que fue crucificado. Ha sido resucitado; no está aquí. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí está el lugar donde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pusieron.
es.R: Pero él les dijo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. {{plural_you:Buscan|Buscáis}} a Jesús de Nazaret, al que mataron en una cruz. ¡Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha resucitado de la muerte! No está aquí. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, aquí está el lugar donde pusieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo.

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Msishangae. Yesu Mnazareti mnamtafuta, yule aliyesulubiwa. Amefufuliwa; hayupo hapa. Angalieni mahali walipomlaza.
sw.B: Lakini yeye aliwaambia, "Msishtuke. Mmekuja kumtafuta Yesu wa Nazareti, aliyesulubiwa. Amefufuliwa; hayupo hapa. Tazameni, hapa ndipo walipomlaza.
sw.R: Lakini yeye aliwaambia, "Msiogope. Mnamtafuta Yesu wa Nazareti, aliyeuawa msalabani. Mungu amemfufua kutoka kwa wafu! Hayupo hapa. Tazameni, hapa ndipo walipoweka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: he has been raised: a passive, God raised him
alternatives: he has risen by his own power
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Jesus spoke of being raised in 14:28.

decisions.choice: the one who has been crucified: a perfect participle, the crucified one
alternatives: the one who was once crucified and is no longer
decisions.reason: The form describes him by what happened to him and what it made him: he is still the crucified one, now raised.

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
alternatives: a member of a group called Nazarenes
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his hometown in Galilee (1:9, 1:24, 14:67).

decisions.choice: see the place: the empty ledge where the body had lain
decisions.reason: The women had watched where he was laid (15:47). The young man shows them the place, now empty.

decisions.choice: God has raised him from death; his body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised him, as the passive implies, and says "from death". It also says "killed on a cross" for "crucified".

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the verbs addressed to the women (se asombren|os asombréis, buscan|buscáis, vean|ved)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: A Jesús el nazareno buscan
decisions.reason: Spanish can put the object first, as the Greek does, so Literal keeps Jesus's name at the front.

decisions.choice: Yesu Mnazareti mnamtafuta
decisions.reason: Swahili can put the object first, with the object prefix -m- in the verb, so Literal keeps Jesus's name at the front, as the Greek does.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε, καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But go, say to the disciples of him and to the Peter that he goes before you into the Galilee; there him you will see, as he said to you.

en.L: But go, tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and Peter that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you."
en.B: But go and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and Peter too, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is going on ahead of you to Galilee. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to you."
en.R: Now go and tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, and be sure to tell Peter too. Tell them, 'Jesus is going to Galilee ahead of you. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you.'"

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:vayan|id}}, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y a Pedro que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} precede a Galilea; allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, conforme {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo».
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:digan|decid}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y también a Pedro, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} va camino de Galilea antes que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo».
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:vayan|id}} y {{plural_you:avisen|avisad}} a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores, y no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de decírselo también a Pedro. {{plural_you:Díganles|Decidles}}: “Jesús va a Galilea antes que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}, tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo”».

sw.L: Lakini nendeni, waambieni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na Petro kwamba anatangulia mbele yenu kwenda Galilaya; mtamwona huko, sawasawa na alivyowaambia."
sw.B: Lakini nendeni mkawaambie wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na Petro pia, kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anaenda Galilaya kabla yenu. Mtamwona huko, kama alivyowaambia."
sw.R: Sasa nendeni mkawaambie wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na msisahau kumwambia Petro pia. Waambieni, 'Yesu anakwenda Galilaya kabla yenu. Mtamwona huko, kama alivyowaambia.'"

decisions.choice: as he told you: Jesus' promise on the way to the Mount of Olives (14:28)
decisions.reason: In 14:28 Jesus said, "After I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee." The promise is now kept.

decisions.choice: and Peter: Peter is named because he had denied Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter denied Jesus three times (14:66-72). Naming him here shows that he is not shut out.

decisions.choice: goes before you: leads the way, as a shepherd before his flock
decisions.reason: In 14:27-28 the promise follows the saying about the scattered sheep. Jesus will gather them again in Galilee.

decisions.choice: that: introduces the message, which may be read as direct speech
decisions.reason: The word can mark a reported message or the words to be spoken. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: be sure to tell Peter; Tell them
alternatives: tell his disciples and Peter that
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the message as the women's own words and stresses that Peter is to hear it.

decisions.choice: los precede
decisions.reason: "Preceder" is one verb for going ahead of someone, as the Greek is, and keeps the picture of leading the way (meaning decision m3).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν, ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out they fled from the tomb, had seized for them trembling and amazement; and to none nothing they said, they were afraid for.

en.L: And going out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
en.B: They went out and ran from the tomb, trembling and beside themselves. And they told no one anything, for they were afraid.
en.R: The women went out and ran away from the tomb. They were shaking and could hardly think. They did not tell anyone anything, because they were afraid.

es.L: Y saliendo, huyeron del sepulcro, pues temblor y asombro se habían apoderado de ellas; y a nadie dijeron nada, pues tenían miedo.
es.B: Salieron y huyeron del sepulcro, temblorosas y fuera de sí. Y no dijeron nada a nadie, porque tenían miedo.
es.R: Las mujeres salieron y se fueron corriendo de la tumba. Temblaban y apenas podían pensar. No le contaron nada a nadie, porque tenían miedo.

sw.L: Na walipotoka, walikimbia kutoka kaburini, kwa kuwa kutetemeka na mshangao vilikuwa vimewashika; na hawakumwambia yeyote chochote, kwa kuwa waliogopa.
sw.B: Walitoka, wakakimbia kutoka kaburini, wakitetemeka na kupigwa na butwaa. Hawakumwambia mtu yeyote jambo lolote, kwa sababu waliogopa.
sw.R: Wale wanawake walitoka, wakakimbia mbali na kaburi. Walikuwa wakitetemeka, na hawakuweza hata kufikiri vizuri. Hawakumwambia mtu yeyote chochote, kwa sababu waliogopa.

decisions.choice: the Gospel ends at 16:8 in the earliest manuscripts; the endings that follow are later additions, printed by the SBLGNT in double brackets
decisions.reason: The two oldest complete manuscripts of the New Testament, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, both from the fourth century, end Mark at 16:8 with "for they were afraid". Most manuscripts, nearly all of them later, go on with 16:9-20, the longer ending. Its style and vocabulary differ from the rest of Mark: many of its words occur nowhere else in the Gospel, it introduces Mary Magdalene in 16:9 as if she had not just been named in 16:1, and its appearances read like a summary of those told in Luke, John and Acts. Some manuscripts have instead a short ending after 16:8 (the women report briefly to Peter's companions, and Jesus sends out through them the proclamation of eternal salvation), and a few have the short ending followed by the longer one. The SBLGNT prints both endings after 16:8 in double brackets, which mark a passage that was not part of the original text but is old and widely read. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an open question: Mark may have ended here on purpose, or his ending may have been lost
decisions.reason: Whether Mark meant to end at 16:8 or his first ending was lost is an open question. A book ending on the word "for", with the women silent and afraid, is very unusual, and it leaves the meeting promised in 16:7 untold. Some think the last page of the earliest copy was lost or never written. Others think Mark ended here on purpose: the promise of 16:7 stands, the reader knows the message was later told, and the silence leaves the reader facing the empty tomb. The later endings show that early copyists felt the Gospel needed a fuller close. The manuscripts cannot settle the question. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: for they were afraid: the Greek sentence ends with the word for
decisions.reason: A Greek sentence may end with "for", and short sentences like this one do occur. But no other book is known to end that way, which is part of the question about Mark's ending.

decisions.choice: trembling and amazement: shaking with fear and beside themselves with awe
decisions.reason: The second word means being out of oneself with astonishment, as in 5:42. Fear and awe are the response to God's power in Mark (4:41; 5:15).

decisions.choice: they said nothing to anyone: two negatives together, a strong statement
decisions.reason: Greek piles up negatives for emphasis. They told no one on the way. The message itself was later told, or the story would not be known.

decisions.choice: beside themselves (B); could hardly think (R)
decisions.reason: The word means being out of oneself. Balanced and Readable say so in plain words. Both keep "afraid" as the last word, as the Greek ends with fear.

decisions.choice: pues tenían miedo, at the end
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence ends with the word for "for" (meaning decision m3). Spanish cannot end a sentence with "pues" in this sense, so Literal ends with the fear, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kupigwa na butwaa (struck with stupor)
decisions.reason: "Beside themselves": the Greek word is amazement that leaves a person unable to think (meaning decision m4). "Mshangao" is ordinary surprise; "butwaa" is being dumbfounded.

source.text: Πάντα δὲ τὰ παρηγγελμένα τοῖς περὶ τὸν Πέτρον συντόμως ἐξήγγειλαν.

records.literal_gloss: All now the things having been commanded to those around the Peter briefly they reported.

en.L: And all the things commanded they reported briefly to those around Peter.
en.B: They gave Peter and those with him a short report of all they had been told.
en.R: The women quickly told Peter and the others with him everything the young man had told them to say.

es.L: Y todo lo mandado lo anunciaron brevemente a los que [estaban] alrededor de Pedro.
es.B: Contaron brevemente a Pedro y a los que estaban con él todo lo que se les había encargado.
es.R: Las mujeres contaron en pocas palabras a Pedro y a los demás que estaban con él todo lo que el joven les había mandado decir.

sw.L: Basi mambo yote yaliyoagizwa waliwapasha kwa ufupi wale [waliokuwa] pamoja na Petro.
sw.B: Wakawaeleza Petro na wenzake kwa ufupi yote waliyokuwa wameagizwa.
sw.R: Wale wanawake waliwaeleza Petro na wenzake kwa maneno machache yote ambayo yule kijana aliwaagiza kusema.

decisions.choice: the short ending: found in some manuscripts after 16:8, printed by the SBLGNT in double brackets as not part of the original text
decisions.reason: This ending is found in a few manuscripts, mostly after 16:8 and before the longer ending; one Latin manuscript has it alone. Its words and style are not Mark's, and it seems written to round off a Gospel that ended at 16:8. It contradicts 16:8, where the women say nothing to anyone. See the notes on 16:8. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: briefly: in few words
decisions.reason: The word usually means concisely; it can also mean promptly. Either way the report was short and soon made.

decisions.choice: those around Peter: Peter and the disciples with him
decisions.reason: The phrase means Peter's group, the disciples named in 16:7.

decisions.choice: the things commanded: the young man's message in 16:7
decisions.reason: The women report what they were told to say.

decisions.choice: The women; everything the young man had told them to say
alternatives: all the things commanded they reported
decisions.reason: Readable names the women and the one who gave them the message. It reads "briefly" as "quickly", one sense of the word.

decisions.choice: en pocas palabras
decisions.reason: The adverb means "in few words" (meaning decision m2, uncertain). The English Readable says "quickly"; Spanish Readable keeps the sense that Literal and Balanced give, "brevemente".

decisions.choice: kwa maneno machache (in few words)
decisions.reason: The adverb means "in few words" (meaning decision m2, uncertain). The English Readable says "quickly"; Swahili Readable keeps the sense that Literal and Balanced give, "kwa ufupi".

source.text: μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς καὶ ἄχρι δύσεως ἐξαπέστειλεν δι’ αὐτῶν τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἄφθαρτον κήρυγμα τῆς αἰωνίου σωτηρίας.

records.literal_gloss: After now these things also himself the Jesus from east and as far as west sent out through them the holy and imperishable proclamation of the eternal salvation.

en.L: And after these things Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} also sent out through them, from [the] east even to [the] west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.
en.B: After this Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} sent out through them, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation.
en.R: After that, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} used them to send out the holy message of eternal salvation from the east to the west. It is a message that will never pass away.

es.L: Y después de estas cosas, también el mismo Jesús envió por medio de ellos, desde [el] oriente hasta [el] occidente, la sagrada e incorruptible proclamación de la salvación eterna.
es.B: Después de esto, el propio Jesús envió por medio de ellos, de oriente a occidente, el anuncio sagrado e imperecedero de la salvación eterna.
es.R: Después de eso, Jesús mismo los usó para llevar el santo mensaje de la salvación eterna desde el oriente hasta el occidente. Es un mensaje que nunca pasará.

sw.L: Na baada ya mambo haya, Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} pia alituma kupitia wao, kutoka mashariki hata magharibi, tangazo takatifu lisiloharibika la wokovu wa milele.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alituma kupitia kwao, kutoka mashariki hadi magharibi, tangazo takatifu lisiloweza kuharibika la wokovu wa milele.
sw.R: Baada ya hapo, Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliwatumia kupeleka ujumbe mtakatifu wa wokovu wa milele kutoka mashariki hadi magharibi. Ni ujumbe ambao hautapita kamwe.

decisions.choice: from east to west: through the whole world
decisions.reason: The rising and setting of the sun stand for the whole earth (Psalm 113:3; Malachi 1:11).

decisions.choice: imperishable: that cannot decay or die
decisions.reason: The word is used of God (Romans 1:23) and of the resurrection body (1 Corinthians 15:52). The message is undying.

decisions.choice: proclamation: the message preached, the announcement of Jesus
decisions.reason: The word names the content of what was preached, as in 1 Corinthians 1:21.

decisions.choice: eternal salvation: rescue that lasts forever
decisions.reason: The phrase is found in Hebrews 5:9. It is not a phrase Mark uses, which is one sign that this ending comes from a later hand.

decisions.choice: a message that will never pass away
decisions.reason: Readable explains "imperishable" in a separate sentence and uses "message" for the proclamation.

decisions.choice: el mismo Jesús (L); el propio Jesús (B); Jesús mismo (R), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: English "himself" is a pronoun and takes the setting. Spanish says it with an adjective beside the name, "mismo" or "propio", which is not a pronoun, so there is nothing for the setting to capitalise.

source.text: ἀμήν.

en.L: Amen.
en.B: Amen.
en.R: Amen.

es.L: Amén.
es.B: Amén.
es.R: Amén.

sw.L: Amina.
sw.B: Amina.
sw.R: Amina.

decisions.choice: amen: so be it, a closing word of agreement
alternatives: truly, at the start of a saying
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the word to begin solemn sayings ("Truly I say to you"). Here it closes the short ending as a prayer or a reading in church is closed.

decisions.choice: Amen
decisions.reason: The word is kept as it is, since it is used in English worship with the same sense.

source.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.

records.literal_gloss: Having risen now early on [the] first [day] of the week he appeared first to Mary the Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

en.L: Now having risen early on [the] first [day] of the week, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had cast out seven demons.
en.B: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had risen, early in the morning of the first day of the week, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} first to Mary Magdalene. It was from her that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had thrown out seven demons.
en.R: Jesus rose from death early on Sunday morning. He showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} first to Mary from Magdala. Before this, Jesus had forced seven demons to leave her.

es.L: Ahora bien, resucitado temprano el primer [día] de la semana, se mostró primero a María Magdalena, de quien había expulsado siete demonios.
es.B: Después de resucitar, temprano en la mañana del primer día de la semana, se mostró primero a María Magdalena. Era de ella de quien había echado fuera siete demonios.
es.R: Jesús resucitó el domingo muy temprano. Se mostró primero a María, la de Magdala. Antes de esto, Jesús había obligado a siete demonios a salir de ella.

sw.L: Basi, akiwa amefufuka mapema siku ya kwanza ya juma, alionekana kwanza na Mariamu Magdalene, ambaye kutoka kwake alikuwa amefukuza pepo saba.
sw.B: Baada ya kufufuka asubuhi na mapema siku ya kwanza ya juma, alijionyesha kwanza kwa Mariamu Magdalene. Huyo ndiye ambaye alikuwa amewafukuza pepo saba kutoka kwake.
sw.R: Yesu alifufuka Jumapili asubuhi na mapema. Alijionyesha kwanza kwa Mariamu wa Magdala. Kabla ya hapo, Yesu alikuwa amewalazimisha pepo saba kumtoka.

decisions.choice: 16:9-20, the longer ending: found in most manuscripts but not in the earliest; printed by the SBLGNT in double brackets
decisions.reason: The two oldest complete manuscripts of the New Testament, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, both from the fourth century, end Mark at 16:8 with "for they were afraid". Most manuscripts, nearly all of them later, go on with 16:9-20, the longer ending. Its style and vocabulary differ from the rest of Mark: many of its words occur nowhere else in the Gospel, it introduces Mary Magdalene in 16:9 as if she had not just been named in 16:1, and its appearances read like a summary of those told in Luke, John and Acts. Some manuscripts have instead a short ending after 16:8 (the women report briefly to Peter's companions, and Jesus sends out through them the proclamation of eternal salvation), and a few have the short ending followed by the longer one. The SBLGNT prints both endings after 16:8 in double brackets, which mark a passage that was not part of the original text but is old and widely read. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an open question: Mark may have ended at 16:8 on purpose, or his ending may have been lost
decisions.reason: Whether Mark meant to end at 16:8 or his first ending was lost is an open question. A book ending on the word "for", with the women silent and afraid, is very unusual, and it leaves the meeting promised in 16:7 untold. Some think the last page of the earliest copy was lost or never written. Others think Mark ended here on purpose: the promise of 16:7 stands, the reader knows the message was later told, and the silence leaves the reader facing the empty tomb. The later endings show that early copyists felt the Gospel needed a fuller close. The manuscripts cannot settle the question. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene, freed from seven demons: as in Luke 8:2; the first to see him, as in John 20:11-18
alternatives: a new person in the story
decisions.reason: Luke 8:2 says seven demons had gone out of her. John 20:11-18 tells how the risen Jesus met her at the tomb.

decisions.choice: early on the first day: goes with having risen, and also sets the time of the appearance
decisions.reason: The time phrase stands between the two verbs. Either way he rose and appeared that same Sunday morning.

decisions.choice: seven demons: a complete and severe possession
decisions.reason: Seven is often a number of fullness. Mark does not tell this story elsewhere.

decisions.choice: thrown out (B); forced to leave (R)
decisions.reason: The pattern of earlier chapters for driving out demons. Readable also names Jesus and says "from death".

source.text: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: She having gone told [it] to those with him having been, mourning and weeping;

en.L: She went and told [it] to those who had been with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as they were mourning and weeping;
en.B: She went and brought the news to the people who had been with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who were grieving and weeping.
en.R: She went and told the people who had been with Jesus. They were very sad and crying.

es.L: Ella fue y [lo] anunció a los que habían estado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que estaban de luto y llorando;
es.B: Ella fue y dio la noticia a los que habían estado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que estaban de duelo y llorando.
es.R: Ella fue y se lo contó a los que habían estado con Jesús. Estaban muy tristes y lloraban.

sw.L: Yeye alikwenda, akawaarifu wale waliokuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, waliokuwa wakiomboleza na kulia;
sw.B: Alikwenda, akawaletea habari wale waliokuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, ambao walikuwa wakiomboleza na kulia.
sw.R: Alikwenda, akawaambia watu waliokuwa pamoja na Yesu. Walikuwa na huzuni nyingi, wakilia.

decisions.choice: those who had been with him: his disciples and close followers
decisions.reason: The phrase is wider than the eleven, though it includes them (3:14).

decisions.choice: mourning and weeping: grieving aloud for the dead
decisions.reason: The two words describe open grief, the mourning for the dead that was customary.

decisions.choice: the people who had been with Jesus
alternatives: those who had been with him
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since the pronoun alone could be unclear.

source.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they having heard that he lives and was seen by her disbelieved.

en.L: And they, hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive and had been seen by her, disbelieved.
en.B: But on hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alive and that she had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they would not believe it.
en.R: The followers heard that Jesus was alive and that Mary had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But they did not believe her.

es.L: Y ellos, al oír que vivía y que había sido visto por ella, no [lo] creyeron.
es.B: Pero al oír que estaba vivo y que ella {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había visto, no quisieron creerlo.
es.R: Los seguidores oyeron que Jesús estaba vivo y que María {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había visto. Pero no le creyeron.

sw.L: Na hao waliposikia kwamba yu hai na kwamba ameonwa naye, hawakuamini.
sw.B: Lakini waliposikia kwamba yu hai, na kwamba yeye mwenyewe amemwona, hawakukubali kuamini.
sw.R: Wafuasi walisikia kwamba Yesu yu hai na kwamba Mariamu amemwona. Lakini hawakumwamini.

decisions.choice: disbelieved: refused to believe
decisions.reason: The verb is the opposite of believe. Unbelief runs through this ending (16:13, 16:14, 16:16).

decisions.choice: he is alive: present tense, the words of the report
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the message: he lives.

decisions.choice: would not believe (B); did not believe (R)
decisions.reason: The single English word is stiff. Balanced and Readable use the verb believe with a negative.

source.text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν·

records.literal_gloss: After now these things to two of them walking he appeared in another form, going into [the] country;

en.L: And after these things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country;
en.B: After that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared to two of them in a different form, as they were walking along on their way into the country.
en.R: Later, Jesus appeared to two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers while they were walking out into the country. He looked different from before.

es.L: Y después de estas cosas, se apareció en otra forma a dos de ellos que iban caminando, mientras iban al campo;
es.B: Después de esto se apareció con otro aspecto a dos de ellos, que iban de camino al campo.
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús se apareció a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores mientras caminaban hacia el campo. Tenía un aspecto diferente al de antes.

sw.L: Na baada ya mambo haya, aliwatokea wawili kati yao kwa sura nyingine walipokuwa wakitembea, wakienda mashambani;
sw.B: Baadaye aliwatokea wawili kati yao kwa sura tofauti, walipokuwa wakitembea njiani kwenda mashambani.
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu aliwatokea wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wawili walipokuwa wakitembea kwenda mashambani. Alionekana tofauti na hapo awali.

decisions.choice: two of them walking into the country: the story told in Luke 24:13-35
decisions.reason: Luke tells how the risen Jesus walked with two disciples on the road to Emmaus.

decisions.choice: in another form: in a form they did not at first recognize
alternatives: in a body other than his own
decisions.reason: In Luke 24:16 their eyes were kept from recognizing him. The phrase does not say what changed.

decisions.choice: the country: the open land outside the city
decisions.reason: They were leaving Jerusalem for the countryside.

decisions.choice: He looked different from before
decisions.reason: Readable puts the phrase in a sentence of its own and names Jesus and his followers.

source.text: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς· οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they having gone away told [it] to the rest; not even them did they believe.

en.L: And they went away and told [it] to the rest; they did not believe them either.
en.B: These two went back and told the others, but they did not believe them either.
en.R: These two went back and told the other followers. But the others did not believe them either.

es.L: Y ellos fueron y [lo] anunciaron a los demás; tampoco a ellos creyeron.
es.B: Estos dos volvieron y se lo contaron a los demás, pero tampoco a ellos les creyeron.
es.R: Estos dos regresaron y se lo contaron a los otros seguidores. Pero los otros tampoco les creyeron.

sw.L: Nao wakaenda zao, wakawaarifu wale wengine; wala hawakuwaamini hao pia.
sw.B: Hao wawili walirudi, wakawaambia wale wengine, lakini hawakuwaamini wao pia.
sw.R: Hao wawili walirudi, wakawaambia wafuasi wengine. Lakini wale wengine hawakuwaamini wao pia.

decisions.choice: they did not believe them either: the rest did not believe the two, as they had not believed Mary
alternatives: the two did not believe the rest
decisions.reason: The subject changes. The rest are the ones who did not believe, as in 16:11.

decisions.choice: unbelief: set beside Luke 24:33-35
decisions.reason: In Luke 24:34 the eleven greet the two with the news that the Lord has appeared to Simon. This ending tells it differently and stresses the disciples' unbelief.

decisions.choice: These two; the other followers; the others
decisions.reason: Readable names who is who, since "they" refers first to the two and then to the rest.

source.text: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Later now reclining they the eleven he appeared, and rebuked the unbelief of them and hardness of heart because those having seen him having been raised not they believed.

en.L: And later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining [at table], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been raised.
en.B: Later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appeared to the eleven themselves as they were eating. He rebuked them for their unbelief and their stubborn hearts, because they had not believed those who had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} risen.
en.R: Later Jesus appeared to the eleven apostles while they were eating a meal. He scolded them because they did not believe and their hearts were stubborn. They had not believed the people who saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alive again.

es.L: Y más tarde se apareció a los once mismos mientras estaban recostados [a la mesa], y les reprochó su incredulidad y dureza de corazón, porque no habían creído a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían visto resucitado.
es.B: Más tarde se apareció a los once mismos mientras comían. Les reprochó su incredulidad y la dureza de su corazón, porque no habían creído a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían visto resucitado.
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús se apareció a los once apóstoles mientras comían. Los regañó porque no creían y porque eran tercos de corazón. No habían creído a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron vivo otra vez.

sw.L: Na baadaye aliwatokea wale kumi na mmoja wenyewe walipokuwa wameegemea [mezani], akawakemea kwa kutoamini kwao na ugumu wa mioyo yao, kwa sababu hawakuwaamini wale waliomwona amefufuliwa.
sw.B: Baadaye aliwatokea wale kumi na mmoja wenyewe walipokuwa wakila. Akawakemea kwa kutoamini kwao na kwa ukaidi wa mioyo yao, kwa sababu hawakuwaamini wale waliomwona akiwa amefufuka.
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu aliwatokea wale mitume kumi na mmoja walipokuwa wakila chakula. Aliwakaripia kwa sababu hawakuamini, na mioyo yao ilikuwa migumu. Hawakuwaamini watu waliomwona akiwa hai tena.

decisions.choice: reclining: lying at table on couches, the custom at a meal
decisions.reason: At formal meals people lay on couches around a low table, leaning on one arm (14:18).

decisions.choice: the eleven: the twelve without Judas
decisions.reason: Judas had handed Jesus over (14:10, 14:43). The group is still called by its number.

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: a mind closed and unwilling
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought and will, as in 3:5, 6:52 and 8:17.

decisions.choice: the text of the SBLGNT, without the addition after 16:14
alternatives: add a long reply of the disciples and Jesus' answer after 16:14
decisions.reason: One fifth-century manuscript, Codex Washingtonianus, adds a passage after this verse in which the disciples excuse their unbelief and Jesus answers them. It is found nowhere else. Some manuscripts also add "from the dead" after "raised". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: eating (B, R); stubborn hearts (B); their hearts were stubborn (R)
alternatives: reclining at table; hardness of heart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what reclining at table means and use "stubborn" for the hard heart. Readable says "apostles" to name the eleven and "scolded" for rebuked.

decisions.choice: wameegemea [mezani] (reclining [at table])
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision m1). "Kuegemea" is to lean or recline; Literal keeps the posture and brackets the table, as the English does. Balanced and Readable say they were eating.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Having gone into the world all proclaim the gospel to all the creation.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Going into all the world, proclaim the gospel to the whole creation.
en.B: He told them, "Go out into the whole world and announce the gospel to all of creation.
en.R: Jesus told them, "Go everywhere in the world. Tell the good news to every person.

es.L: Y les dijo: «Yendo por todo el mundo, {{plural_you:proclamen|proclamad}} el evangelio a toda la creación.
es.B: Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} al mundo entero y {{plural_you:anuncien|anunciad}} el evangelio a toda la creación.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a todas partes del mundo. {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} la buena noticia a todas las personas.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Mkienda katika ulimwengu wote, hubirini Injili kwa viumbe vyote.
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Nendeni katika ulimwengu mzima, mkaitangaze Injili kwa viumbe vyote.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Nendeni kila mahali ulimwenguni. Wapelekeeni watu wote habari njema.

decisions.choice: the world: the whole inhabited earth, all its peoples
decisions.reason: Here the word means the earth and everyone in it, as in 14:9, where the gospel is to be proclaimed in all the world.

decisions.choice: all the creation: every human being
decisions.reason: The gospel is preached to people. The phrase means everyone, everywhere, as in Colossians 1:23.

decisions.choice: the command to proclaim: compare Matthew 28:19-20 and Mark 13:10
decisions.reason: Jesus said the gospel must first be proclaimed to all nations (13:10). Matthew 28:19 gives the command to make disciples of all nations.

decisions.choice: every person
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who is meant. Readable says "good news" for gospel, as elsewhere.

decisions.choice: el evangelio (L, B); la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "evangelio" names the message at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what the word means, as the English "good news" does.

decisions.choice: Injili (L, B); habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "Injili" names the message at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means, as the English "good news" does.

source.text: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having believed and having been baptized will be saved, the [one] however having disbelieved will be condemned.

en.L: The one who has believed and has been baptized will be saved, but the one who has disbelieved will be condemned.
en.B: Whoever has believed and been baptized will be saved; anyone who refuses to believe will be condemned.
en.R: Those who believe and are baptized will be saved. But those who do not believe will be judged guilty.

es.L: El que ha creído y ha sido bautizado será salvo, pero el que no ha creído será condenado.
es.B: Quien haya creído y haya sido bautizado se salvará; quien se niegue a creer será condenado.
es.R: Los que crean y sean bautizados serán salvados. Pero los que no crean serán declarados culpables.

sw.L: Yeye aliyeamini na kubatizwa ataokolewa, lakini yeye ambaye hakuamini atahukumiwa.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote aliyeamini na kubatizwa ataokolewa; lakini yeyote anayekataa kuamini atahukumiwa.
sw.R: Wale wanaoamini na kubatizwa wataokolewa. Lakini wale wasioamini watahukumiwa kuwa na hatia.

decisions.choice: believed and baptized: faith and baptism belong together; the negative names unbelief alone
alternatives: baptism is required for salvation in every case
decisions.reason: The second half does not say "not baptized". It is unbelief that brings condemnation.

decisions.choice: will be saved: rescued from judgment, at the last day
decisions.reason: The word is used of salvation at the end in 13:13 and of rescue in this life in 5:34. Set against condemnation, it means final rescue.

decisions.choice: condemned: judged guilty and sentenced
decisions.reason: The word means the verdict of a judge (10:33; 14:64).

decisions.choice: refuses to believe (B); do not believe (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the verb believe with a negative. Readable says "judged guilty" for condemned and uses the plural "those who" for the general saying.

source.text: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν, γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς, ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Signs now those having believed these will accompany: in the name of me demons they will cast out, with tongues they will speak new, \v 18 serpents they will take up, and if deadly anything they drink, no not them shall it hurt, upon [the] sick hands they will lay, and well they will be.

en.L: And these signs will accompany those who have believed: in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues; \v 18 they will pick up serpents, and if they drink anything deadly, it will not hurt them at all; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well."
en.B: These signs will go with those who believe: they will throw out demons in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and speak in new tongues; \v 18 they will lift up snakes; if they swallow any deadly poison, it will do them no harm; they will put their hands on those who are sick, and the sick will get better."
en.R: And these signs will be seen with those who believe. They will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to force demons to leave people. They will speak in new languages. \v 18 They will pick up snakes. If they drink some poison that kills, it will not hurt them. They will put their hands on sick people, and the sick people will get well."

es.L: Y a los que han creído los acompañarán estas señales: en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre expulsarán demonios; con lenguas nuevas hablarán; \v 18 alzarán serpientes, y si beben algo mortal, en ningún modo les dañará; impondrán las manos a los enfermos, y estos estarán bien».
es.B: Estas señales acompañarán a los que crean: en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre expulsarán demonios y hablarán en lenguas nuevas; \v 18 levantarán serpientes; si tragan algún veneno mortal, no les hará ningún daño; pondrán las manos sobre los enfermos, y estos se recuperarán».
es.R: Y estas señales se verán en los que crean. Usarán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para obligar a los demonios a salir de las personas. Hablarán en idiomas nuevos. \v 18 Levantarán serpientes con las manos. Si beben algún veneno que mata, no les hará daño. Pondrán las manos sobre los enfermos, y los enfermos se sanarán».

sw.L: Na ishara hizi zitaandamana na wale walioamini: kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} watawafukuza pepo; watanena kwa ndimi mpya; \v 18 nyoka watawainua, na hata wakinywa kitu chochote chenye kuua, hakitawadhuru hata kidogo; mikono wataiweka juu ya wagonjwa, nao watakuwa wazima."
sw.B: Ishara hizi zitakuwa pamoja na wale wanaoamini: watawafukuza pepo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na watanena kwa ndimi mpya; \v 18 watawabeba nyoka mikononi; wakimeza sumu yoyote ya kuua, haitawadhuru; wataweka mikono yao juu ya wagonjwa, na wagonjwa hao watapona."
sw.R: Na ishara hizi zitaonekana kwa wale wanaoamini. Watatumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kuwalazimisha pepo kuwatoka watu. Watazungumza kwa lugha mpya. \v 18 Watawashika nyoka mikononi. Wakinywa sumu inayoua, haitawadhuru. Wataweka mikono yao juu ya wagonjwa, nao wagonjwa watapona."

decisions.choice: signs: acts of power that point to God at work
decisions.reason: In 8:11-12 Jesus refused to give a sign to those who demanded one. Here signs follow the preaching and confirm it (16:20).

decisions.choice: the signs: each is told of the apostles in Acts
decisions.reason: Demons are cast out (Acts 16:18), believers speak in tongues (Acts 2:4; 10:46), Paul is bitten by a snake and not harmed (Acts 28:3-6), and the sick are healed by the laying on of hands (Acts 28:8). There is no story of drinking poison in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: new tongues: speech given by the Spirit, in languages not learned
decisions.reason: In Acts 2:4-11 the disciples speak in other languages. Paul speaks of tongues as speech in the Spirit (1 Corinthians 14:2). The verse does not say which is meant.

decisions.choice: if they drink anything deadly: a promise of protection, not a command to test God
decisions.reason: The sentence is a condition: if it happens, they will not be harmed. Jesus refused to test God by putting himself in danger (Matthew 4:5-7).

decisions.choice: they will pick up serpents, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: and with their hands they will pick up serpents
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "and with their hands". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: languages
decisions.reason: Readable uses "languages" for the word that also means the tongue in the mouth. Readable also uses "force demons to leave people", as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: ndimi (L, B); lugha (R)
decisions.reason: As the English "tongues" and "languages": "ndimi" (tongues) keeps the Greek word and the familiar phrase "kunena kwa ndimi"; Readable says "lugha", languages not learned (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν κύριος Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς ἀνελήμφθη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The indeed therefore Lord Jesus after the speaking to them was taken up into the heaven and sat at [the] right hand of God.

en.L: So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at [the] right hand of God.
en.B: So the Lord Jesus, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat at the right hand of God.
en.R: After the Lord Jesus finished talking to them, God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up into heaven. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down at God's right side, the place of highest honor.

es.L: Así pues, el Señor Jesús, después de hablarles, fue llevado arriba al cielo y se sentó a [la] diestra de Dios.
es.B: Así que el Señor Jesús, después de haberles hablado, fue elevado al cielo y tomó asiento a la derecha de Dios.
es.R: Cuando el Señor Jesús terminó de hablarles, Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó arriba al cielo. Allí se sentó a la derecha de Dios, el lugar de mayor honor.

sw.L: Basi, Bwana Yesu, alipokwisha kuzungumza nao, alipandishwa juu mbinguni, akaketi upande wa kulia wa Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Bwana Yesu, alipomaliza kusema nao, alichukuliwa juu mbinguni, akaketi kwenye kiti {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} upande wa kulia wa Mungu.
sw.R: Bwana Yesu alipomaliza kuzungumza nao, Mungu alimchukua juu mbinguni. Huko aliketi upande wa kulia wa Mungu, mahali pa heshima kuliko pote.

decisions.choice: sat at the right hand of God: the words of Psalm 110:1
alternatives: only a picture of being near God
decisions.reason: Jesus quoted Psalm 110:1 in 12:36 and used its words before the high priest in 14:62. To sit at a king's right hand is to share his rule and honor.

decisions.choice: was taken up: a passive, God took him up
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Elijah (2 Kings 2:11) and of Jesus in Acts 1:2, 1:11.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus: Jesus named as Lord
alternatives: Lord as a polite title, sir
decisions.reason: Mark's own narrative does not call Jesus "the Lord Jesus". The full title belongs to the early church's preaching (Acts 1:21).

decisions.choice: God took him up; the place of highest honor
alternatives: was taken up; at the right hand
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who took him up, as the passive implies, and explains what the right hand means.

decisions.choice: upande wa kulia
decisions.reason: "Kulia" is the everyday word for right; "kuume" is older. "Upande" (side) says where he sat, as at the women's "upande wa kulia" in verse 5.

source.text: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν πανταχοῦ, τοῦ κυρίου συνεργοῦντος καὶ τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος διὰ τῶν ἐπακολουθούντων σημείων.

records.literal_gloss: They now having gone out proclaimed everywhere, the Lord working with [them] and the word confirming by the accompanying signs.

en.L: And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with [them] and confirmed the word through the signs that accompanied [it].
en.B: And they went out and proclaimed the message everywhere. The Lord worked with them and confirmed the word by the signs that came with it.
en.R: Then the followers went out and told the message everywhere. The Lord worked with them. He proved that their message was true by the signs that happened along with it.

es.L: Y aquellos salieron y proclamaron en todas partes, mientras el Señor cooperaba con [ellos] y confirmaba la palabra mediante las señales que [la] acompañaban.
es.B: Y ellos salieron y proclamaron el mensaje por todas partes. El Señor actuaba con ellos y confirmaba la palabra con las señales que la acompañaban.
es.R: Entonces los seguidores salieron y anunciaron el mensaje por todas partes. El Señor trabajaba con ellos. Por medio de las señales que acompañaban el mensaje, demostraba que era verdadero.

sw.L: Na hao walitoka, wakahubiri kila mahali, huku Bwana akishirikiana [nao] na kulithibitisha neno kupitia ishara zilizoandamana [nalo].
sw.B: Nao walitoka, wakatangaza ujumbe kila mahali. Bwana alifanya kazi pamoja nao, akalithibitisha neno kwa ishara zilizoandamana nalo.
sw.R: Kisha wafuasi walitoka, wakawaambia watu ujumbe huo kila mahali. Bwana alifanya kazi pamoja nao. Alionyesha kwamba ujumbe wao ni wa kweli kwa ishara zilizotokea pamoja na ujumbe huo.

decisions.choice: the word: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: As in 2:2 and 4:14, "the word" means the message that is preached.

decisions.choice: confirming: showing to be true and reliable
decisions.reason: The verb was used of guarantees in law and business. The signs back up the message (Hebrews 2:3-4).

decisions.choice: the Lord worked with them: the risen Lord at work in their preaching
alternatives: they worked for the Lord, apart from him
decisions.reason: Though taken up into heaven, the Lord still acts with them.

decisions.choice: signs, the end of the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen" at the end of the Gospel. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the message (B, R); the followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they proclaimed. Readable names who went out and says "proved that their message was true" for confirmed.
